text:
maya: Quick proposal — add an optional `priority_hint` field to the rerank request envelope (enum: interactive|background|bulk). It drives routing (low-latency vs low-cost) + quota classification + console breakdown.

sam: +1 on having explicit hints. saves us guessing from client patterns.

lee: how do we prevent clients from always saying `interactive` to get better models?

maya: good call. plan: priority_hint doesn't bypass quota; it maps to quota buckets and cost multipliers. interactive = higher per-unit cost and stricter rate caps; background = cheaper units, higher latency targets. abuse is addressed by quota enforcement and sampling for mismatch.

raj: we need telemetry to detect mismatches between hint and observed latency/throughput. e.g., if client marks interactive but 95p latency > 500ms, flag and mark for ops review.

maya: agreed. propose adding `observed_priority_score` metric and a `hint_discrepancy` tag emitted by the reranker service.

ops-bot: canary deployed: rerank-priority-hint-v1 -> 8% traffic (PR #4123).

lee: what about backward compatibility? many clients send existing envelope. default mapping?

maya: default = unspecified->treated as `background` for now to avoid surprise cost spikes. we can change default later with notice.

sam: dashboard UX: we should surface a per-route "priority distribution" and top offenders for hint_discrepancy. PMs want this for debugging regressions.

tina: I'll mock a Console tile: time-series of requests by priority_hint, stacked by model variant, with a small table of top tenants with discrepancy rate.

raj: also add a sampling probe that records full input length and model chosen for 0.1% of requests so we can correlate candidate counts with cost.

lee: scoring format changes? do we need to add provenance fields on individual scores to indicate which model produced them?

maya: yes — add `score_provenance` on candidate objects: model_tag + quantization_tag + optional fallback_reason. helps trace degrades.

sam: example request idea:
```json
{
  "request_id": "r-123",
  "priority_hint": "interactive",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "..."},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "..."}
  ]
}
```

maya: example response snippet:
```json
{
  "ranks": [
    {"id":"c2","score":0.87,"score_provenance":"v2-quant8:fallback-none"},
    {"id":"c1","score":0.12,"score_provenance":"v2-quant8:fallback-none"}
  ],
  "model_variant": "v2-quant8",
  "routing_decision": "pinned-low-latency"
}
```

lee: fallback_reason could be useful for console notifications when a higher-fidelity model timed out. But be careful with PII — ensure reason doesn't echo candidate text.

maya: noted. fallback_reason = enum {none, timeout, capacity, degraded_quality} + optional internal_tag for ops only.

raj: telemetry naming: use stable metric names: `rerank.requests_by_priority`, `rerank.hint_discrepancy_rate`, `rerank.score_provenance.count`. add a trace attribute `priority_hint` so traces can be aggregated easily.

sam: ops implications: routing policy table needs new column for `allowed_tiers` and `cost_multiplier`. who owns rollout?

maya: infra + platform will own serving changes, devex + console for telemetry + UI. let's schedule a short canary checklist: 1) telemetry emits, 2) console tile exists (mock ok), 3) quota mapping applied, 4) rollback plan.

tina: mock will be ready by EOD Wednesday. I'll add a small "why this matters" blurb for PMs.

ops-bot: noted: rollback hook added to canary (manifest rerank-priority-hint-v1).

lee: one more: quota math for mixed requests (some tenants send both bulk and interactive) — we need clear docs showing unit conversion.

maya: I'll draft the policy doc with conversion table and example invoice lines. will ping engineering for review.

sam: thanks. if no objections, I'll land the schema change and telemetry bits as a feature flag behind canary.

lee: no objections from me. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — filing RFC after the canary metrics look good.
